messages.subject: RW2 at irregular locations
parts:
I'm interested in applying a RW2 over age groups at irregular locations: 15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20-24, 25-29, ... 45-49

I see the disucssion at this post in 2012: https://groups.google.com/forum/embed/?parenturl=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.r-inla.org%2Fcomments-1&service=jotspot&ul=1&theme=default&place=forum%2Fr-inla-discussion-group&showpopout=true&showsearch=true#!searchin/r-inla-discussion-group/rw2$20irregular/r-inla-discussion-group/VJ0zjSFnTyA/cODcTUzfiSgJ

1) Is this the correct approach for smoothing over irregularly sized age groups?
2) Have there been any pertinent updates to the code since then?

Thanks.

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] RW2 at irregular locations
parts:
RW1 and RW2 handle correctly irregular locations. I recommend adding

scale.model=TRUE

to make them scale, so that the precision means the same.

using

f(time, model="rw2", values = time.points)

the the argument 'values' defines the timepoints the rw2 is defined. by
default its eq to unique(sort(time))

and you can add more points there than in 'time',

like
time.points = 1:100

and time =c(1,2,10,50,80)

messages.author: 9940b4fcc153c7d7
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] RW2 at irregular locations
parts:
I notice that you write the interval 20-24 and not the value 22. With the normal indexed RW2 model, you have to select a certain point that is representative of the interval (e.g. the median of the interval).

If you instead want the average of "rw2 at age 20, rw2 at age 21, rw2 at age 22, rw2 at age 23, rw2 at age 24", that can be done with the stack functionality and the A matrix.

Best,
Haakon
